targeted_two_block_review.james_1938_scope: Original article inaccessible. Later primary Dietmann-Elsholtz authorpp1-2 attributes exact three-summand Gaussian split support and a binary approximation allowing at most two bad prime factors per summand. This confirms relevance but neither excludes the full original nor supplies the arbitrary-form two-block asymptotic.
targeted_two_block_review.squarefree_finite_sieve_diagnostic: Fixed SL2 block basis changes can arrange coordinate-unit solutions at finitely many bad primes, so the direct local-range counterexample alone does not exclude an indirect deduction. However the available elementary large-gcd tail is O_epsilon(N^(1+epsilon)/P), not uniform O(N/P); a fixed cutoff followed by N tending to infinity does not suffice. Growing cutoffs require coefficient/progression uniformity beyond the cited fixed-form statements. No impossibility of adapting their proofs is asserted.
